newsitem.title: USA: M-Wave sells operation, sees Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: M-Wave sells operation, sees Q4 loss.

text.p: M-Wave Inc said Thursday it sold its assembly operations on December 13, and expects the company's fourth quarter after-tax loss to increase by about $150,000 or $0.05 a share as a result of the sale.
The amount of inventory write-downs has not yet been determined and will depend on certain anticipated price adjustments and scrap levels, M-Wave said.
Terms of the sale were not disclosed, and the company could not be reached for further information.

M-Wave said it expects to report fourth quarter results in early February. In November, the company said it expected to report lower sales and a loss for the fourth quarter but did not specify how much. In the third quarter, the company lost $0.07 a share versus a loss of $0.16 for the period last year.

"In the context of our strategic repositioning we took this opportunity to sell our assembly operation, which no longer fit into our long-term strategy," said Joe Turek, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement. He added that M-Wave's best opportunity for sustainable growth and profitability is in complex printed circuit boards for high frequency applications.
M-Wave manufactures microwave printed circuit boards, used in various industrial and military applications.
